axis.definition: The number line's axis: its range from min to max, and optionally its tick spacing and whether its ticks are labeled.

barColor.definition: The color of every bar, unless a category gives its own: a color name or a hex code such as #0072b2.

categories.definition: The categories, drawn in the order given: at least 1 and at most 100, each with a different name.

categoryAxisLabel.definition: A label for the axis that lists the categories, as plain text, at most 200 characters. In the drawing, a label longer than two lines is cut short with “…”; the text alternative states it whole.

circumference.definition: The distance around the circle, 2π times the radius, from 0.006 to 6,283,186.

circumferenceLabelText.definition: Text shown in place of the circumference label, at most 200 characters, such as "r" or "?"; it also labels the circumference. It replaces the whole label, unit included, so add the unit to the text if it should show. An empty text is a blank label, for example a space to fill in. Text too long to fit beside the figure is placed below it, and text longer than four lines is cut short with “…”. The text alternative still states the value.

color.definition: The color of this one point, segment, bar or measured object: a color name or a hex code such as #0072b2.

diameter.definition: The distance across the circle through its center, twice the radius, from 0.002 to 2,000,000.

diameterLabelText.definition: Text shown in place of the diameter label, at most 200 characters, such as "r" or "?"; it also labels the diameter. It replaces the whole label, unit included, so add the unit to the text if it should show. An empty text is a blank label, for example a space to fill in. Text too long to fit beside the figure is placed below it, and text longer than four lines is cut short with “…”. The text alternative still states the value.

end.definition: The ruler mark the object ends at, after its start, given as the start is.

from.definition: Where a line segment starts: its x and y coordinates.

guideLines.definition: Whether a three-dimensional coordinate graph draws dashed guide lines from each point straight to the x,y plane, and from there to the x-axis and the y-axis, so the point's depth can be read; off unless true.

label.definition: A label for this one point, segment or measured object, as plain text, at most 200 characters. In the drawing, a long label is cut short with “…”; the text alternative states it whole.

labelCircumference.definition: Whether the circumference is labeled with its measurement, next to the circle.

labelDiameter.definition: Whether the diameter is labeled with its measurement; a labeled diameter is drawn.

labelRadius.definition: Whether the radius is labeled with its measurement; a labeled radius is drawn.

labelSides.definition: Which sides are labeled with the side length: one side (the bottom) or all four. Without it, no side is labeled unless sideLabelText is given.

leftArrow.definition: Whether the number line's left end has an arrowhead, showing the line goes on; shown unless false. Without one, the line stops at its min.

length.definition: How many whole units a ruler is long: 1 to 30 for centimeters, 1 to 12 for inches.

lineColor.definition: The color of a line: the number line itself, a figure's outline, or one series of a line graph. A color name or a hex code such as #0072b2.

lineLabel.definition: A label for a line: the number line itself, or one series of a line graph, as plain text, at most 200 characters. In the drawing, a label longer than two lines is cut short with “…”: below a number line, or in a line graph's legend. The text alternative states it whole.

max.definition: The highest value on an axis: negative, zero or positive, whole or decimal, from -1000000000 to 1000000000, and above the axis's min by at least a billionth of the larger end's size (and at least 0.000000001).

maximum.definition: The highest value on the value axis, from -1000000000 to 1000000000: 0, or at least 0.000000001 in size; above the minimum by at least a billionth of the larger end's size.

measuredObject.definition: An object lying along the ruler, to be measured, drawn as a bar from its start mark to its end mark; its length is never written on the figure.

min.definition: The lowest value on an axis: negative, zero or positive, whole or decimal, from -1000000000 to 1000000000, and below the axis's max.

minimum.definition: The lowest value on the value axis, from -1000000000 to 1000000000: 0, or at least 0.000000001 in size.

name.definition: The category's name, as plain text, at most 200 characters. A long name wraps onto more lines.

orientation.definition: Which way the categories' rows, columns or bars run: horizontal or vertical. The default is horizontal for a pictograph and vertical for a bar graph.

points.definition: The points marked on the graph, each at its position (its value on a number line, its x and y on a coordinate graph) and optionally with a label and a color. Points may share a position: each is drawn, and their labels are placed apart where the drawing has room.

radius.definition: The distance from the center to the circle, from 0.001 to 1,000,000.

radiusLabelText.definition: Text shown in place of the radius label, at most 200 characters, such as "r" or "?"; it also labels the radius. It replaces the whole label, unit included, so add the unit to the text if it should show. An empty text is a blank label, for example a space to fill in. Text too long to fit beside the figure is placed below it, and text longer than four lines is cut short with “…”. The text alternative still states the value.

rightArrow.definition: Whether the number line's right end has an arrowhead, showing the line goes on; shown unless false. Without one, the line stops at its max.

rulerUnit.definition: The unit a ruler is marked in: centimeters or inches.

segments.definition: The line segments drawn on a coordinate graph, at most 1000, each from one point to another, and optionally with a label at its middle and a color.

series.definition: The series, at least 1 and at most 6, each drawn as a line through one point per category. Without a lineColor, a series takes the default color for its position (the first series the first color, and so on); every series also has its own point shape and dash pattern, so series differ without color.

showCenter.definition: Whether the center is marked with a point.

showDiameter.definition: Whether the diameter is drawn through the center; it never lies on the radius.

showGrid.definition: Whether a coordinate graph has grid lines across it at every tick of both axes; off unless true.

showRadius.definition: Whether the radius is drawn, from the center horizontally to the right.

showRightAngles.definition: Whether the four right angles are marked, with a small right-angle mark in each corner.

showTickLabels.definition: Whether an axis's ticks are labeled with their values; shown unless false. A label shows no more decimal places than the tick spacing needs.

showValues.definition: Whether to write each bar's value beside it, exactly as given; a zero bar shows 0.

sideLabelText.definition: Text shown in place of the side label, at most 200 characters, such as "s" or "?"; given alone it labels one side, and with labelSides "all" it labels all four sides. It replaces the whole label, unit included, so add the unit to the text if it should show. An empty text is a blank label, for example a space to fill in. Text too long to fit beside the figure is placed below it, and text longer than four lines is cut short with “…”. The text alternative still states the value.

sideLength.definition: The length of each side of the square, from 0.001 to 1,000,000.

smallestDivision.definition: The smallest division an inch ruler is marked to; sixteenth when left out.

start.definition: The ruler mark the object starts at, in the ruler's unit, as a decimal: a whole millimeter on a centimeter ruler (3.4), a multiple of the smallest division on an inch ruler (2.0625 for 2 1/16). Any mark from 0 to the ruler's length.

text.definition: The text written at a tick in place of its value, as plain text, at most 200 characters. An empty text leaves the tick unlabeled. In the drawing, a text wider than its tick's room is cut short with “…”, though never to fewer than a few letters, so on a densely ticked line neighbouring labels may touch; the text alternative states it whole.

tickInterval.definition: The distance between neighbouring ticks on the value axis: greater than 0, dividing the scale into whole intervals, with at most 100 ticks.

tickLabels.definition: Custom labels written at ticks in place of their values, at most 100: for example "start" at 0, or a blank at a tick to fill in. When two labels share a tick, the first is written. Hidden with the other tick labels when the axis's showTickLabels is false.

tickSpacing.definition: The distance between neighbouring ticks on an axis: greater than 0 and at most 2000000000, giving at most 100 ticks. Ticks fall at every whole multiple of it inside the range, so zero is always ticked when the range includes it, and an end that is not a multiple has no tick. When it is left out, the spacing is 1, 2 or 5 times a power of ten, chosen to give between 5 and 20 ticks on a range at least 0.001 wide (fewer on a narrower one), or coarser, down to two ticks, where the axis is drawn too short for its tick labels to stand apart.

title.definition: A title shown above the graph, as plain text, at most 200 characters. In the drawing, a title longer than three lines is cut short with “…”; the text alternative states it whole.

to.definition: Where a line segment ends: its x and y coordinates.

type.definition: The graph type: which kind of graph the description draws.

unit.definition: The unit of length shown after each measurement, such as cm, at most 20 characters. A unit with sentence punctuation is quoted in the text alternative.

unitImage.definition: The picture every unit is drawn with, by name from the published image set.

unitValue.definition: How many units one picture stands for: greater than 0, at most 1000000000.

value.definition: A position on the number line, in the line's own numbers: where a point is marked, or the tick a custom label is written at. It must lie on the line's range, ends included; a custom label's value must be a tick.

valueAxisLabel.definition: A label for the axis that shows the values, as plain text, at most 200 characters. In the drawing, a label longer than two lines is cut short with “…”; the text alternative states it whole.

valueScale.definition: The value axis's scale: its minimum, maximum and tick interval, each optional. A part that is given is used exactly and never extended, and must include every value; a part left out is chosen to fit the data: the minimum is zero, or lower for a line graph's negative values, and the axis ends on a tick.

valueUnitLabel.definition: What one unit of value counts, as plain text, at most 200 characters, such as "students"; the key names the picture, as in "each apple = 2 students". Left out, empty or blank, it says "units". In the drawing, a key longer than two lines is cut short with “…”; the text alternative states the label whole.

values.definition: One value per category, in the same order as the categories.

version.definition: The schema version the description is written for. Leave it out for the current version, 1.

x.definition: The x coordinate of a point: of a plotted point or, on an x,y graph, a segment's end, in the x-axis's own numbers and inside its range, ends included; or of a triangle's vertex, from -1,000,000 to 1,000,000.

xAxis.definition: The coordinate graph's x axis: its range from min to max, and optionally its tick spacing and whether its ticks are labeled.

xAxisLabel.definition: A label for the x-axis, as plain text, at most 200 characters.

y.definition: The y coordinate of a point: of a plotted point or, on an x,y graph, a segment's end, in the y-axis's own numbers and inside its range, ends included; or of a triangle's vertex, from -1,000,000 to 1,000,000, with y increasing upward.

yAxis.definition: The coordinate graph's y axis: its range from min to max, and optionally its tick spacing and whether its ticks are labeled.

yAxisLabel.definition: A label for the y-axis, as plain text, at most 200 characters.

z.definition: A position along the z-axis, in its own numbers: a point's z coordinate, inside the z-axis range, ends included.

zAxis.definition: The three-dimensional coordinate graph's upright z axis: its range from min to max, and optionally its tick spacing and whether its ticks are labeled.

zAxisLabel.definition: A label for the z-axis, as plain text, at most 200 characters.

number-line.title: Number line
number-line.description: A number line: one axis from its min to its max, negative, positive or across zero, with ticks, an arrowhead at each end unless turned off, and optionally marked points (at most 100), custom tick labels and a label for the line.
checks: the axis range can be drawn
the axis tick spacing is greater than 0 and gives at most 100 ticks
every point lies on the number line's range
every custom tick label is at a tick

ruler.title: Ruler
ruler.description: A ruler in centimeters or inches, drawn to scale with itself (not at true physical size), with whole units numbered from 0, and optionally an object lying along it from one mark to another, for "how long is it?" questions. A centimeter ruler is up to 30 cm long and an inch ruler up to 12 in.

valueDescriptions.centimeters: Numbered every centimeter, with a mark at every millimeter and longer marks at each half centimeter.
valueDescriptions.inches: Numbered every inch, with a mark at every multiple of the smallest division, graded by fraction.

valueDescriptions.eighth: Marks at every eighth of an inch.
valueDescriptions.sixteenth: Marks at every sixteenth of an inch.

checks: the length fits the ruler's unit
the measured object's start is a mark of the ruler
the measured object's end is a mark of the ruler
the measured object's start mark is before its end mark

xy-graph.title: x,y coordinate graph
xy-graph.description: A coordinate graph: an x-axis and a y-axis, each through the origin when the other's range includes zero and along the nearest edge otherwise, showing one, two or four quadrants, one unit drawn the same length on both axes; optionally a grid, points (at most 1000) and line segments (at most 1000).
checks: the xAxis range can be drawn
the xAxis tick spacing is greater than 0 and gives at most 100 ticks
the yAxis range can be drawn
the yAxis tick spacing is greater than 0 and gives at most 100 ticks
every point lies inside both axis ranges
every segment end lies inside both axis ranges
every segment joins two different points

xyz-graph.title: x,y,z coordinate graph
xyz-graph.description: A three-dimensional coordinate graph: an x-axis, a y-axis and a z-axis meeting at the origin (or, for a range without zero, at its end nearest zero), drawn in isometric projection, the same fixed view as cubes and cylinders: z straight up the page, x toward the lower left and y toward the lower right, each 30° below the horizontal, the three 120° apart. Each axis is drawn the same length whatever its range. Points (at most 1000) are plotted at their x, y and z, optionally with dashed guide lines to the x,y plane.
checks: the xAxis range can be drawn
the xAxis tick spacing is greater than 0 and gives at most 100 ticks
the yAxis range can be drawn
the yAxis tick spacing is greater than 0 and gives at most 100 ticks
the zAxis range can be drawn
the zAxis tick spacing is greater than 0 and gives at most 100 ticks
every point lies inside all three axis ranges

line-graph.title: Line graph
line-graph.description: A line graph: one or more series of values over the categories, each value a point and each series a line joining its points, with a legend when there is more than one series. Each series has its own color, point shape and dash pattern. Values may be negative. At most 100 categories and 6 series.
checks: categories are given, each with a different name
one value per category in every series
every series has a different name
the value-scale tick interval is greater than 0
every series value fits the value scale

bar-graph.title: Bar graph
bar-graph.description: A bar graph: one bar per category, upright (the default) or across, its length in exact proportion to the category's value, from zero. Values are 0 or more. At most 100 categories.

valueDescriptions.vertical: Upright bars rising from the value axis, names below (the default).
valueDescriptions.horizontal: Bars across, growing to the right, names on the left.

checks: categories are given, each with a different name
one value per category
the value-scale tick interval is greater than 0
every value fits the value scale
the value scale starts at or below zero

pictograph.title: Pictograph
pictograph.description: A pictograph: one row of pictures per category (or one column, upright), each picture standing for a number of units, with a key such as "each apple = 2 students". A value that is not a whole number of pictures ends in one cropped picture. At most 100 categories and 400 pictures in all.

valueDescriptions.apple: A red apple with a short brown stem and a green leaf.
valueDescriptions.ball: A round blue ball with two curved white stripes.
valueDescriptions.book: A closed purple book seen from the front, with its pages showing at the side.
valueDescriptions.fish: An orange fish facing left, with a tail, a top fin and one dark eye.
valueDescriptions.flower: A flower with five pink petals, a yellow center and a green stem with one leaf.
valueDescriptions.person: A simple figure of a person: a round head above a rounded body, in dark grey.
valueDescriptions.tree: A tree with a brown trunk and a round green crown.

valueDescriptions.horizontal: One row of pictures per category, names on the left (the default).
valueDescriptions.vertical: One upright column of pictures per category, names below.

checks: categories are given, each with a different name
one value per category
the pictures drawn stay within the limit

circle.title: Circle
circle.description: A circle drawn to scale from its radius, diameter or circumference (give one; any other given must agree within 1%). The radius, the diameter and the center can be drawn, and each measurement labeled with its value and unit or with custom text.
checks: radius label text needs the radius labeled
diameter label text needs the diameter labeled
circumference label text needs the circumference labeled
a labeled radius is drawn
radius label text draws the radius
a labeled diameter is drawn
diameter label text draws the diameter

square.title: Square
square.description: A square drawn to scale from its side length. One side or all four can be labeled with the length and unit or with custom text, and its right angles can be marked.

valueDescriptions.one: Label one side, the bottom side, with the side length.
valueDescriptions.all: Label all four sides with the side length.
